cfu.question: Part A is TAP REST TAP TAP. What happens on beat 2, and how long does it last?
cfu.answer: No sound for one full beat; point or move silently while counting.
cfu.decision: If every pupil can show this, fade spoken counting. If anyone compresses the rest, model one full silent beat, practise together, then check individually.

hinge.question: Part A repeats. After beat 4, which action comes on the next equal beat? A: TAP on the new 1. B: Wait an extra beat. C: Start faster.
hinge.answer: A: TAP on the new 1. The repeat has the same pulse.
hinge.decision: All choose at once. If all identify A and demonstrate the boundary, move to independent work. Otherwise count eight equal beats with pointing, add the score, then check the parallel question.

parallel_hinge.decision: Ask each pupil to show the boundary. Keep the visible pulse support for anyone who needs it; log the actual help.

cfu.question: A rests on 2. B taps on 2. Should A add a tap there to match B?

hinge.question: You lose your place while the other part continues. A: Play faster to catch up. B: Follow silently and rejoin on the next 1 cue. C: Make the other part stop.
hinge.answer: B. Keep the shared pulse and use a clear re-entry point.

slides.title: Read and count
lines: Read A or B. Point to your taps and rests.
Wait for the count-in. Play your part with the other part.
slides.notes: 0–15 seconds Show A: TAP REST TAP TAP and B: REST TAP REST TAP. Point down the same numbered column in both scores. Explain: “The parts differ, but the beat positions line up.” 15–30 seconds Give a shared 1, 2, 3, 4 count-in. Play A while the adult helper points B silently. On a second cycle the helper taps B. Keep the common pointer steady. 30–45 seconds Model losing the place without blaming anyone. Stop your sound, follow the boxes silently and rejoin on the next beat 1 cue. Do not race to catch up or interrupt the other part. 45–60 seconds The listener says: “The shared tap on beat 4 came at two times.” Choose: “We will watch beat 4 and keep the pulse.” Try both parts again, then ask whether the tap coincided. This is a class model, not recorded pupil progress.

slides.title: Words for our part
lines: pulse — The even beats shared by both parts.
rehearse — Practise a part so it becomes more secure.
cue — A clear signal that tells us when to act.
feedback — A useful comment about what happened and what to try.
